title: How Do AI Search Engines Impact SEO?
excerpt: AI answers can reduce clicks and shrink shortlists, but SEO still matters. Learn how AI search changes SEO and how to measure your brand's AI visibility.
author: AI Brand Track Team
content:
## Quick Answer

AI search engines impact SEO by answering questions directly, which [can reduce clicks to websites](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/), and by naming a short list of brands instead of ranking ten links. Traditional SEO still matters: [Google says](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) its standard SEO best practices apply to AI Overviews and AI Mode, and assistants that search the web, like ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini, can only cite pages they can find. What changes is how you measure success. Brands now need to track whether AI answers mention them, not just where their pages rank.

## Introduction

Your brand could be missing from the answers your buyers read. You may rank well on Google while AI assistants answer questions about your category without mentioning you.

Traditional search engines return links. AI search returns answers. If your brand isn't part of the answer, you may lose the buyer before they ever reach your website.

These assistants synthesize information and can recommend specific brands. ChatGPT, for example, draws on its [training data](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed) and on [live web search](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt). In our experience, how widely independent sources discuss your brand also shapes the answer.

## What Are AI Search Engines and How Do They Impact SEO?

AI search engines are conversational tools that generate direct answers instead of link lists. ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google Gemini use large language models to understand questions, combine information and give recommendations. Google also adds AI-generated answers to its own results through [AI Overviews and AI Mode](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features).

Unlike a results page, an AI answer doesn't display your title tag or meta description. It paraphrases what sources say about you, or leaves you out.

That changes the goal. Traditional SEO focuses on ranking pages for keywords. AI search optimization, often called [generative engine optimization](/generative-engine-optimization) or GEO, focuses on being cited, mentioned and recommended in AI answers. The term was formalized in a [2023 research paper on Generative Engine Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735), which describes how generative engines synthesize information from multiple sources and how little control content creators have over when and how their content is shown.

## Why Do AI Search Engines Impact SEO Differently Than Google's Classic Results?

AI answers are produced differently from a ranked list, and that affects strategy.

### How Do AI Platforms Choose What to Say?

An AI assistant answers from what its model learned in training and, when it searches, from pages it retrieves at the time. [ChatGPT search](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), for example, may rewrite a user's question into one or more targeted queries sent to search partners, then cite the sources it used.

Classic SEO signals still play a role, because assistants that search the web need to find your pages. But in our experience, the answer also reflects how consistently independent sources describe your brand.

A page can rank first on Google and still go unmentioned by ChatGPT if other sources, such as review sites, comparisons and articles, shape the answer more.

### What Is the Zero-Click Problem in AI Search?

When users get a complete answer on the page, fewer of them click through to websites.

Research on Google's AI summaries quantifies this. [Pew Research Center](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/) analyzed the browsing of 900 US adults in March 2025. Users who saw an AI summary clicked a traditional search result in 8% of visits, compared with 15% for users who didn't. They clicked a link inside the summary itself in just 1% of visits. About 18% of the Google searches in the study produced an AI summary.

Conversational assistants can have a similar effect. For example, when someone asks ChatGPT for project management software recommendations, the answer may already include comparisons, so they may never visit your site.

Traffic alone becomes an incomplete measure. You also need to track AI visibility: how often and how favorably AI answers mention you.

### How Does Conversational Query Intent Change SEO Strategy?

People ask AI assistants full questions, the way they'd ask a knowledgeable colleague.

"Best project management software" becomes "What project management tool should I use for a remote team of 15 people?" The question includes context, constraints and specific needs.

Your content needs to answer these specific questions clearly. That means depth, concrete detail and demonstrated expertise, rather than surface-level keyword targeting.

## Why Does AI Search Engine Impact on SEO Matter Now?

AI answers now appear both inside Google's results (about 18% of the Google searches in [Pew Research Center's study](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/) produced an AI summary) and in standalone assistants.

The practical consequences:

**Fewer clicks for some queries**: As the [Pew data](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/) shows, AI summaries reduce clicks to traditional results.

**Shorter shortlists**: In our experience, AI answers typically name a handful of options. Being one of them matters more than being on page one.

**Less visibility into what happened**: Search Console shows impressions and clicks, but we're not aware of any tool from the AI providers that tells you whether ChatGPT or Claude mentioned your brand.

### What Business Outcomes Connect to AI Search Visibility?

AI visibility connects to business outcomes in a few ways, though attribution is still imperfect:

**Consideration**: If an AI assistant includes your brand in its shortlist, you're in the running. If not, some buyers may not look further.

**Context**: Buyers who arrive after reading an AI answer may already know what you do and why you might fit.

**Competitive position**: When AI names a few brands and you're one of them while competitors aren't, that's an advantage that doesn't show up in rankings.

### How Are Search Behaviors Shifting to AI Platforms?

Conversational, AI-generated answers are now available in many places: Google shows [AI Overviews and AI Mode](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) alongside its traditional results, [ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt) and [Claude](https://claude.com/resources/articles/web-search) both offer web search with citations, and Perplexity [surfaces and links websites in its search results](https://docs.perplexity.ai/guides/bots).

Usage likely differs by audience, and some people use more than one assistant. In our view, the safest assumption is that some of your buyers use each of them.

## How Can You Optimize Your SEO Strategy for AI Search Engines?

Optimizing for AI search builds on traditional SEO rather than replacing it.

### Step 1: Audit Your Current AI Visibility

You can't improve what you don't measure. Start with your current presence across AI platforms.

Ask ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google Gemini questions your buyers ask. Does your brand appear? How often? In what context?

Document 20 to 30 questions about your industry, product category and use cases. Track which platforms mention your brand and which don't. Use fresh conversations and repeat key questions, because in our experience answers vary between runs.

In our experience, it's common to find a gap between a brand's Google rankings and its AI visibility.

### Step 2: Build Authority Signals

Focus on what makes a brand easy for AI to recommend.

Publish genuinely useful, expert content: detailed guides, original research and real customer examples. Thin posts written for keywords add little.

Earn mentions in respected publications in your industry. Coverage on independent sites can help both search rankings and the sources AI assistants draw on.

Keep your brand description, pricing and positioning consistent across your site, profiles and listings. Conflicting information makes it harder for AI to describe you accurately.

### Step 3: Structure Content for AI and Search

Make your content easy to understand for people, search engines and AI systems alike.

Use clear headings that reflect the structure of the topic.

Answer questions directly. Each section should make sense on its own, because an AI answer may draw on a specific passage rather than a whole page.

Add structured data where it applies. [Google's introduction to structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data) explains how markup helps it understand page content. Note that Google says there are [no additional requirements or special optimizations](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) needed to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode; its standard SEO best practices apply.

Make sure the crawlers you want can reach your pages. OpenAI, for example, documents [OAI-SearchBot and its other crawlers](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots), which webmasters can manage through robots.txt.

### Step 4: Create Content for Conversational Questions

Create content that answers the natural-language questions buyers actually ask.

Find those questions: talk to your sales and support teams, review "People also ask" boxes, and look at the questions in your own site search and support tickets.

Write complete answers with context, examples and practical guidance. Generic answers rarely stand out.

Cover specific scenarios and edge cases. Content about specific use cases often matches conversational questions better than broad overviews. See [how to rank on ChatGPT](/how-to-rank-on-chatgpt) for more on this.

### Step 5: Build a Consistent Presence Across Sources

AI visibility depends on your presence across the sources these systems learn from and retrieve.

Build relationships with industry publications, podcasts and newsletters. Being mentioned and linked helps.

Take part genuinely in industry discussions on Reddit, forums and professional networks.

Contribute expert content to respected sites in your space.

### Step 6: Monitor and Adapt as Platforms Change

AI platforms change often. Providers release new models, retire old ones and add features; the [ChatGPT release notes](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes) show how often.

Re-check your visibility on a regular schedule. A sudden drop may reflect a platform change, a new competitor or a content gap.

Test new content formats and topics based on what you learn.

Follow provider announcements, such as the [ChatGPT release notes](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes), so you know when something changed.

## Frequently Asked Questions About How AI Search Engines Impact SEO

### Do AI search engines completely replace traditional SEO?

No. [Google says](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) its standard SEO best practices apply to its AI features, and assistants that search the web still need to find your pages. You need both: strong SEO and an understanding of how AI answers describe your brand. See [GEO vs SEO vs AEO](/blog/geo-vs-seo-vs-aeo) for how the disciplines fit together.

### How quickly can brands improve their AI search visibility?

There's no reliable fixed timeline. Answers based on live web search can change once new or updated pages are being retrieved, which can be relatively quick. Answers drawn from a model's training data may only change with a future model version. Ongoing effort and regular measurement matter more than any single change.

### Which AI platform should brands prioritize?

In our view, ChatGPT is a sensible starting point for most brands, but Claude, Perplexity and Gemini each have their own audiences. The underlying work (useful content, credible coverage, accurate information) helps across all of them, so it's worth measuring every platform rather than optimizing for just one.

### Can small businesses compete with enterprise brands in AI search?

Often, yes, especially for specific questions. A small business with deep expertise in a niche and clear content about specific use cases can be mentioned for questions that match it closely. In our experience, broad category questions still tend to favor brands with more coverage.

### How do you measure ROI from AI search optimization?

Track AI visibility metrics such as mention rate, sentiment and share of voice against competitors over time, alongside referral traffic from AI platforms and conversions. Add an AI option to "how did you hear about us" forms. Attribution is still imperfect, so look at trends rather than precise ROI figures.

### What content types perform best in AI search results?

Detailed guides, original research, real customer examples, expert analysis and honest comparison content tend to be most useful, because they give AI systems specific, credible information to draw on. Thin content written only for keywords rarely helps. Google's guidance on [helpful, people-first content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) is a good benchmark.

### How often do AI platforms change?

Often. Providers release new models, retire old ones and change search features (see the [ChatGPT release notes](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes)), and in our testing answers vary between runs anyway. Treat AI visibility as an ongoing measurement, not a one-time project.

## Conclusion: Take Control of Your AI Search Visibility

How do AI search engines impact SEO? They answer questions directly, reduce clicks for many queries, and narrow buyers' options to a short list of brands. Traditional SEO remains the foundation, but it's no longer the whole picture.

Brands that do well treat AI visibility as a metric alongside rankings and traffic. They check their presence across ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini, create content that answers real buyer questions, and build credible coverage beyond their own site.
